- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon.
- Forecasts show a strong upward bias after recent spikes or volatility, failing to account for mean reversion.
- Model underestimates sharp downward corrections following high peaks (e.g., 45+ → 30–35).
- Forecasts tend to lag behind true price movements, particularly in the first 5–10 days of the forecast window.
- Model exhibits “overshoot” behavior after sharp upward moves — forecasting higher than true price after a spike.
- Forecasts are overly smooth, failing to capture sudden volatility or sharp reversals in the true outcome.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of downward corrections in the second half of the forecast (e.g., 40–45 → 30–35).
- Forecasts show persistent bias toward higher values, especially when true prices exhibit strong downward momentum.
- Model fails to adjust for seasonality or policy-driven volatility (e.g., EU ETS auction cycles) in the short-term forecast.
